questions.question: Describe in outline how a landline call and a mobile call each reach the person being called.
questions.expected_answer: Landline: lifting the handset sends a small current along a pair of copper wires to the local exchange; dialled tones tell the exchange the number; the exchange switches the call through to the other line, via other exchanges and cables if needed; speech travels as a varying electric current and the exchange powers the handset. Mobile: the handset converts speech to a digital signal and transmits it as radio waves to the nearest tower or base station; the tower passes the call by cable or microwave link to the network's switching centre, which connects it to the other party; as the caller moves, the call is handed from tower to tower, each covering an area called a cell.

questions.question: Give three advantages and three disadvantages of mobile telephone systems compared with landlines.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages: a tower serves thousands of users without wiring each house, so coverage spreads quickly and cheaply; the phone travels with its owner, reaching a person rather than a place; it carries many services including messaging, internet and banking, and prepaid airtime suits irregular incomes. Disadvantages: it depends on a charged battery and on signal, which hills, valleys and some buildings block; calls can drop when cells are full or towers lose power or have batteries stolen; handsets are stolen and lost and produce large amounts of e-waste, and towers consume power and affect landscapes.

questions.question: Explain why the comparison between landline and mobile systems does not produce a single winner, using two different users as examples.
questions.expected_answer: Each system has strengths the other lacks, so the better choice depends on the user's needs. A landline works through power cuts, does not drop calls and cannot be lost or stolen in the street, which suits a rural clinic or a grandmother who needs a lifeline when the electricity fails. A mobile goes anywhere with signal, can be bought and topped up in small amounts and carries banking and internet, which suits a trader moving between markets or a learner who needs information. Evaluating a technology means judging it against particular needs, and both systems have earned their place.
